headline: Congress used a special review process to cancel a 2016 Interior Department rule on hunting and wildlife rules in Alaska's national wildlife refuges.
what_it_does: This joint resolution cancels a final rule the Department of the Interior issued on August 5, 2016. That rule covered non-subsistence taking of wildlife and public participation and closure procedures on National Wildlife Refuges in Alaska. Under the Congressional Review Act, the rule is treated as having no legal effect once the resolution becomes law. The official summary does not describe the specific rule provisions in detail.

who_it_affects.group: People who hunt or trap on national wildlife refuges in Alaska
who_it_affects.how: The 2016 rule's hunting and trapping rules for these refuges no longer apply, so the earlier rules remain in place.

who_it_affects.group: Federal wildlife managers at the Department of the Interior and the Fish and Wildlife Service
who_it_affects.how: They must manage Alaska refuges without the 2016 rule and cannot enforce it.

when_it_takes_effect: The resolution took effect when it was signed into law on April 3, 2017.
